enrichment.markdown:
- **Rabbi David Perkowitz (Dovid Perkowitz / Perkovitz; הרב דוד פרקוביץ):** Searches of JewishGen and the permitted Yad Vashem and USHMM collections for these name forms, including “David Perkowitz” and “Dovid Perkowitz,” did not yield a reliable identification of the Jerusalem rabbi. I found no independently verifiable dates, family, occupation, or biography for him; the name alone is not enough to connect him safely to records about other Perkowitz families.

- **Ozhivov Hasidic dynasty and Chmielnik:** I found no outside-archive source that securely connects Rabbi Perkowitz to the Ozhivov household or identifies the particular Ozhivov family in the passage. A useful, but distinct, historical connection is the Ożarów dynasty: a JewishGen memorial-book account says Rabbi Arie Leibish served as rabbi in Chmielnik before settling in Ożarów, and traces the dynasty to Rabbi Leibish Epstein, a student of the Seer of Lublin. It describes Chmielów Hasidim and their congregations in other towns, but does **not** establish that Ożarów and Ozhivov are the same dynasty or that this is the household Rabbi Perkowitz recalled. ([JewishGen, “The Admor of Chmielów”](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/wierzbnik/wie143.html))

- **Rabbi Leib, rabbi of Chmielnik:** The name is too broad to identify a single person without further detail. The Chmielnik history records several rabbis and gives family information for some: for example, Rabbi Dovid Shmuel Shmelka was the son of Rabbi Yehuda Leib of Szydlow and had five brothers. This is a documented rabbinic family, but the source does not establish that he—or his father—is the “Rabbi Leib” meant in the connected record. ([JewishGen, Chmielnik rabbis](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Chmielnik/chm0073.html))

- **Rabbi Jacob Toib of Radokh; Niflaot HaRebbe; Derekh Emunah u-Maaseh Rav:** Searches in JewishGen for the names and title spellings supplied did not produce a dependable match tying them to Perkowitz, the Ozhivov household, or Chmielnik. I cannot assign a biography or publication history on that evidence.

- **Aharon Marcus and *Hasidism*:** A JewishGen memorial-book account identifies Aharon Marcus as a Hamburg-born Hasidic writer and Zionist activist (1843–1916), describes his study and activity among Radomsk Hasidim, and notes that he wrote on Hasidism. This supports the historical context of Hasidic storytelling and transmission, but does not show a personal connection to Perkowitz or the Ozhivov family. ([JewishGen, Radomsko Memorial Book](https://jewishgen.org/yizkor/Radomsko/rad075.html))

- **Jerusalem:** No independent record located identifies this Perkowitz with a particular Jerusalem address, congregation, or family. I found no evidence establishing his migration or life history beyond the memorial-book reference.
